chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man left behind with him: A man left behind with his family an expense of two thousand, for two years, upon which is Zakat. He said: If he was present, then upon him is Zakat, and if he was absent, then there is no Zakat upon it.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat obligatory on wealth left with family if the owner is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'presence' (hudur) in the obligation of Zakat, distinguishing between a resident owner and one who is traveling or absent. Imam al-Rida (AS) rules that Zakat is due on the wealth left with his family if he is considered present (e.g., a local merchant), but exempt if he is absent, reflecting the Shia juristic view that absence can suspend the immediate liability until his return or the wealth's accumulation. This ruling underscores the practical application of Zakat eligibility based on the owner's status and the wealth's stability in his possession.
